verses.original: Σαῦλος δὲ ἦν συνευδοκῶν τῇ ἀναιρέσει αὐτοῦ Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ διωγμὸς μέγας ἐπὶ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τὴν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις πάντες δὲ διεσπάρησαν κατὰ τὰς χώρας τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Σαμαρείας πλὴν τῶν ἀποστόλων
verses.transliteration: Saulos de ēn syneudokōn tē anairesei autou Egeneto de en ekeinē tē hēmera diōgmos megas epi tēn ekklēsian tēn en Hierosolymois pantes de diesparēsan kata tas chōras tēs Ioudaias kai Samareias plēn tōn apostolōn
verses.literal: And Saul was there giving approval to Stephen’s death On that day a great persecution broke out against the church in Jerusalem and all except the apostles were scattered throughout . . . . . . Judea and Samaria
verses.literalPt: E TAMBÉM Saulo consentiu na morte dele. E fez-se naquele dia uma grande perseguição contra a igreja que estava em Jerusalém; e todos foram dispersos pelas terras da Judéia e de Samaria, exceto os apóstolos.

verses.original: συνεκόμισαν δὲ τὸν Στέφανον ἄνδρες εὐλαβεῖς καὶ ἐποίησαν κοπετὸν μέγαν ἐπ’ αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: synekomisan de ton Stephanon andres eulabeis kai epoiēsan kopeton megan ep’ autō
verses.literal: God-fearing men buried Stephen and mourned deeply over him
verses.literalPt: E uns homens piedosos foram enterrar Estêvão, e fizeram sobre ele grande pranto.

verses.original: Σαῦλος δὲ ἐλυμαίνετο τὴν ἐκκλησίαν κατὰ τοὺς οἴκους εἰσπορευόμενος σύρων τε ἄνδρας καὶ γυναῖκας παρεδίδου εἰς φυλακήν
verses.transliteration: Saulos de elymaineto tēn ekklēsian kata tous oikous eisporeuomenos syrōn te andras kai gynaikas paredidou eis phylakēn
verses.literal: But Saul began to destroy the church Going from house to house . . . . . . he dragged off men and women and put them in prison
verses.literalPt: E Saulo assolava a igreja, entrando pelas casas; e, arrastando homens e mulheres, os encerrava na prisão.

verses.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διασπαρέντες διῆλθον εὐαγγελιζόμενοι τὸν λόγον
verses.transliteration: Hoi men oun diasparentes diēlthon euangelizomenoi ton logon
verses.literal: Those who had been scattered preached the word wherever they went
verses.literalPt: Mas os que andavam dispersos iam por toda a parte, anunciando a palavra.

verses.original: Φίλιππος δὲ κατελθὼν εἰς τὴν πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρείας ἐκήρυσσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Χριστόν
verses.transliteration: Philippos de katelthōn eis tēn polin tēs Samareias ekēryssen autois ton Christon
verses.literal: Philip went down to a city in Samaria and proclaimed the Christ to them
verses.literalPt: E, descendo Filipe à cidade de Samaria lhes pregava a Cristo.

verses.original: προσεῖχον δὲ οἱ ὄχλοι τοῖς λεγομένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ Φιλίππου ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐν τῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοὺς καὶ βλέπειν τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐποίει
verses.transliteration: proseichon de hoi ochloi tois legomenois hypo tou Philippou homothymadon en tō akouein autous kai blepein ta sēmeia ha epoiei
verses.literal: The crowds all paid close attention . . . to Philip’s message . . . . . . and to the signs they saw him perform
verses.literalPt: E as multidões unanimemente prestavam atenção ao que Filipe dizia, porque ouviam e viam os sinais que ele fazia;

verses.original: πολλοὶ γὰρ τῶν ἐχόντων πνεύματα ἀκάθαρτα βοῶντα φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἐξήρχοντο πολλοὶ δὲ παραλελυμένοι καὶ χωλοὶ ἐθεραπεύθησαν
verses.transliteration: polloi gar tōn echontōn pneumata akatharta boōnta phōnē megalē exērchonto polloi de paralelymenoi kai chōloi etherapeuthēsan
verses.literal: With loud shrieks unclean spirits came out of many who were possessed and many of the paralyzed and lame were healed
verses.literalPt: Pois que os espíritos imundos saíam de muitos que os tinham, clamando em alta voz; e muitos paralíticos e coxos eram curados.

verses.original: ἐγένετο δὲ πολλὴ χαρὰ ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ
verses.transliteration: egeneto de pollē chara en tē polei ekeinē
verses.literal: So there was great joy in that city
verses.literalPt: E havia grande alegria naquela cidade.

verses.original: Ἀνὴρ δέ τις ὀνόματι Σίμων προϋπῆρχεν ἐν τῇ πόλει μαγεύων καὶ ἐξιστάνων τὸ ἔθνος τῆς Σαμαρείας λέγων εἶναί τινα ἑαυτὸν μέγαν
verses.transliteration: Anēr de tis onomati Simōn proupērchen en tē polei mageuōn kai existanōn to ethnos tēs Samareias legōn einai tina heauton megan
verses.literal: Prior to that time a man named Simon had practiced sorcery in the city and astounded the people of Samaria He claimed . . . to be someone great
verses.literalPt: E estava ali um certo homem, chamado Simão, que anteriormente exercera naquela cidade a arte mágica, e tinha iludido o povo de Samaria, dizendo que era uma grande personagem;

verses.original: ᾧ προσεῖχον πάντες ἀπὸ μικροῦ ἕως μεγάλου λέγοντες Οὗτός ἐστιν ἡ δύναμις τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡ καλουμένη Μεγάλη
verses.transliteration: hō proseichon pantes apo mikrou heōs megalou legontes Houtos estin hē dynamis tou Theou hē kaloumenē Megalē
verses.literal: and all the people from the least to the greatest heeded his words . . . and said This man is the divine power called the Great Power
verses.literalPt: Ao qual todos atendiam, desde o menor até ao maior, dizendo: Este é a grande virtude de Deus.

verses.original: προσεῖχον δὲ αὐτῷ διὰ τὸ ἱκανῷ χρόνῳ ταῖς μαγείαις ἐξεστακέναι αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: proseichon de autō dia to hikanō chronō tais mageiais exestakenai autous
verses.literal: They paid close attention to him because he had astounded them for a long time with his sorcery
verses.literalPt: E atendiam-no, porque já desde muito tempo os havia iludido com artes mágicas.

verses.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἐπίστευσαν τῷ Φιλίππῳ εὐαγγελιζομένῳ περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ ὀνόματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐβαπτίζοντο ἄνδρες τε καὶ γυναῖκες
verses.transliteration: Hote de episteusan tō Philippō euangelizomenō peri tēs basileias tou Theou kai tou onomatos Iēsou Christou ebaptizonto andres te kai gynaikes
verses.literal: But when they believed Philip as he preached the gospel of the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ they were baptized both men and women
verses.literalPt: Mas, como cressem em Filipe, que lhes pregava acerca do reino de Deus, e do nome de Jesus Cristo, se batizavam, tanto homens como mulheres.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Σίμων καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπίστευσεν καὶ βαπτισθεὶς ἦν προσκαρτερῶν τῷ Φιλίππῳ θεωρῶν τε σημεῖα καὶ δυνάμεις μεγάλας γινομένας ἐξίστατο
verses.transliteration: ho de Simōn kai autos episteusen kai baptistheis ēn proskarterōn tō Philippō theōrōn te sēmeia kai dynameis megalas ginomenas existato
verses.literal: Even Simon himself believed and was baptized He followed Philip closely and was astounded by the great signs and miracles he observed . . .
verses.literalPt: E creu até o próprio Simão; e, sendo batizado, ficou de contínuo com Filipe; e, vendo os sinais e as grandes maravilhas que se faziam, estava atônito.

verses.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἀπόστολοι ὅτι δέδεκται ἡ Σαμάρεια τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀπέστειλαν πρὸς αὐτοὺς Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην
verses.transliteration: Akousantes de hoi en Hierosolymois apostoloi hoti dedektai hē Samareia ton logon tou Theou apesteilan pros autous Petron kai Iōannēn
verses.literal: When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God they sent Peter and John to them
verses.literalPt: Os apóstolos, pois, que estavam em Jerusalém, ouvindo que Samaria recebera a palavra de Deus, enviaram para lá Pedro e João.

verses.original: οἵτινες καταβάντες προσηύξαντο περὶ αὐτῶν ὅπως λάβωσιν Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον
verses.transliteration: hoitines katabantes prosēuxanto peri autōn hopōs labōsin Pneuma Hagion
verses.literal: On their arrival they prayed for them to receive the Holy Spirit
verses.literalPt: Os quais, tendo descido, oraram por eles para que recebessem o Espírito Santo

verses.original: οὐδέπω γὰρ ἦν ἐπ’ οὐδενὶ αὐτῶν ἐπιπεπτωκός μόνον δὲ βεβαπτισμένοι ὑπῆρχον εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ
verses.transliteration: oudepō gar ēn ep’ oudeni autōn epipeptōkos monon de bebaptismenoi hypērchon eis to onoma tou kyriou Iēsou
verses.literal: For the Holy Spirit had not yet fallen upon any of them they had simply been . . . baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus
verses.literalPt: (Porque sobre nenhum deles tinha ainda descido; mas somente eram batizados em nome do Senhor Jesus).

verses.original: τότε ἐπετίθεσαν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπ’ αὐτούς καὶ ἐλάμβανον Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον
verses.transliteration: tote epetithesan tas cheiras ep’ autous kai elambanon Pneuma Hagion
verses.literal: Then Peter and John laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Spirit
verses.literalPt: Então lhes impuseram as mãos, e receberam o Espírito Santo.

verses.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Σίμων ὅτι διὰ τῆς ἐπιθέσεως τῶν χειρῶν τῶν ἀποστόλων δίδοται τὸ Πνεῦμα προσήνεγκεν αὐτοῖς χρήματα
verses.transliteration: Idōn de ho Simōn hoti dia tēs epitheseōs tōn cheirōn tōn apostolōn didotai to Pneuma prosēnenken autois chrēmata
verses.literal: When Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands he offered them money
verses.literalPt: E Simão, vendo que pela imposição das mãos dos apóstolos era dado o Espírito Santo, lhes ofereceu dinheiro,

verses.original: λέγων Δότε κἀμοὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην ἵνα ᾧ ἐὰν ἐπιθῶ τὰς χεῖρας λαμβάνῃ Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον
verses.transliteration: legōn Dote kamoi tēn exousian tautēn hina hō ean epithō tas cheiras lambanē Pneuma Hagion
verses.literal: Give me this power as well he said so that everyone on whom . . . I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit
verses.literalPt: Dizendo: Dai-me também a mim esse poder, para que aquele sobre quem eu puser as mãos receba o Espírito Santo.

verses.original: Πέτρος δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν Τὸ ἀργύριόν σου σὺν σοὶ εἴη εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὅτι τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐνόμισας διὰ χρημάτων κτᾶσθαι
verses.transliteration: Petros de eipen pros auton To argyrion sou syn soi eiē eis apōleian hoti tēn dōrean tou Theou enomisas dia chrēmatōn ktasthai
verses.literal: But Peter replied - May your silver perish . . . . . . with you because you thought you could buy the gift of God with money
verses.literalPt: Mas disse-lhe Pedro: O teu dinheiro seja contigo para perdição, pois cuidaste que o dom de Deus se alcança por dinheiro.

verses.original: οὐκ ἔστιν σοι μερὶς οὐδὲ κλῆρος ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ ἡ γὰρ καρδία σου οὐκ ἔστιν εὐθεῖα ἔναντι τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: ouk estin soi meris oude klēros en tō logō toutō hē gar kardia sou ouk estin eutheia enanti tou Theou
verses.literal: You have no part or share in our ministry because your heart is not right before God
verses.literalPt: Tu não tens parte nem sorte nesta palavra, porque o teu coração não é reto diante de Deus.

verses.original: μετανόησον οὖν ἀπὸ τῆς κακίας σου ταύτης καὶ δεήθητι τοῦ Κυρίου εἰ ἄρα ἀφεθήσεταί σοι ἡ ἐπίνοια τῆς καρδίας σου
verses.transliteration: metanoēson oun apo tēs kakias sou tautēs kai deēthēti tou Kyriou ei ara aphethēsetai soi hē epinoia tēs kardias sou
verses.literal: Repent therefore of - your wickedness and pray to the Lord Perhaps He will forgive you for the intent of your heart
verses.literalPt: Arrepende-te, pois, dessa tua iniqüidade, e ora a Deus, para que porventura te seja perdoado o pensamento do teu coração;

verses.original: εἰς γὰρ χολὴν πικρίας καὶ σύνδεσμον ἀδικίας ὁρῶ σε ὄντα
verses.transliteration: eis gar cholēn pikrias kai syndesmon adikias horō se onta
verses.literal: For I see that you are poisoned by bitterness and captive to iniquity
verses.literalPt: Pois vejo que estás em fel de amargura, e em laço de iniqüidade.

verses.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Σίμων εἶπεν Δεήθητε ὑμεῖς ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ πρὸς τὸν Κύριον ὅπως μηδὲν ἐπέλθῃ ἐπ’ ἐμὲ ὧν εἰρήκατε
verses.transliteration: Apokritheis de ho Simōn eipen Deēthēte hymeis hyper emou pros ton Kyrion hopōs mēden epelthē ep’ eme hōn eirēkate
verses.literal: Then Simon answered . . . Pray to the Lord for me so that nothing you have said may happen to me
verses.literalPt: Respondendo, porém, Simão, disse: Orai vós por mim ao Senhor, para que nada do que dissestes venha sobre mim.

verses.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διαμαρτυράμενοι καὶ λαλήσαντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ Κυρίου ὑπέστρεφον εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα πολλάς τε κώμας τῶν Σαμαριτῶν εὐηγγελίζοντο
verses.transliteration: Hoi men oun diamartyramenoi kai lalēsantes ton logon tou Kyriou hypestrephon eis Hierosolyma pollas te kōmas tōn Samaritōn euēngelizonto
verses.literal: And after Peter and John had testified and spoken the word of the Lord they returned to Jerusalem preaching the gospel in many of the Samaritan villages
verses.literalPt: Tendo eles, pois, testificado e falado a palavra do Senhor, voltaram para Jerusalém e em muitas aldeias dos samaritanos anunciaram o evangelho.

verses.original: Ἄγγελος δὲ Κυρίου ἐλάλησεν πρὸς Φίλιππον λέγων Ἀνάστηθι καὶ πορεύου κατὰ μεσημβρίαν ἐπὶ τὴν ὁδὸν τὴν καταβαίνουσαν ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλὴμ εἰς Γάζαν αὕτη ἐστὶν ἔρημος
verses.transliteration: Angelos de Kyriou elalēsen pros Philippon legōn Anastēthi kai poreuou kata mesēmbrian epi tēn hodon tēn katabainousan apo Ierousalēm eis Gazan hautē estin erēmos
verses.literal: Now an angel of the Lord said to Philip Get up and go south to the - desert road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza
verses.literalPt: E o anjo do SENHOR falou a Filipe, dizendo: Levanta-te, e vai para o lado do sul, ao caminho que desce de Jerusalém para Gaza, que está deserta.

verses.original: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἐπορεύθη καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ Αἰθίοψ εὐνοῦχος δυνάστης Κανδάκης βασιλίσσης Αἰθιόπων ὃς ἦν ἐπὶ πάσης τῆς γάζης αὐτῆς ὃς ἐληλύθει προσκυνήσων εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ
verses.transliteration: kai anastas eporeuthē kai idou anēr Aithiops eunouchos dynastēs Kandakēs basilissēs Aithiopōn hos ēn epi pasēs tēs gazēs autēs hos elēlythei proskynēsōn eis Ierousalēm
verses.literal: So he started out and on his way he met an Ethiopian eunuch a court official - in charge of the entire - treasury of Candace queen of the Ethiopians He had gone to Jerusalem to worship
verses.literalPt: E levantou-se, e foi; e eis que um homem etíope, eunuco, mordomo-mor de Candace, rainha dos etíopes, o qual era superintendente de todos os seus tesouros, e tinha ido a Jerusalém para adoração,

verses.original: ἦν τε ὑποστρέφων καὶ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τοῦ ἅρματος αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀνεγίνωσκεν τὸν προφήτην Ἠσαΐαν
verses.transliteration: ēn te hypostrephōn kai kathēmenos epi tou harmatos autou kai aneginōsken ton prophētēn Ēsaian
verses.literal: and on his return was sitting in his chariot reading Isaiah the prophet
verses.literalPt: Regressava e, assentado no seu carro, lia o profeta Isaías.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ τὸ Πνεῦμα τῷ Φιλίππῳ Πρόσελθε καὶ κολλήθητι τῷ ἅρματι τούτῳ
verses.transliteration: Eipen de to Pneuma tō Philippō Proselthe kai kollēthēti tō harmati toutō
verses.literal: The Spirit said to Philip Go over to that chariot and stay by it
verses.literalPt: E disse o Espírito a Filipe: Chega-te, e ajunta-te a esse carro.

verses.original: Προσδραμὼν δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος ἤκουσεν αὐτοῦ ἀναγινώσκοντος Ἠσαΐαν τὸν προφήτην καὶ εἶπεν Ἆρά γε γινώσκεις ἃ ἀναγινώσκεις
verses.transliteration: Prosdramōn de ho Philippos ēkousen autou anaginōskontos Ēsaian ton prophētēn kai eipen Ara ge ginōskeis ha anaginōskeis
verses.literal: So Philip ran up and heard the man reading Isaiah the prophet - Do you understand what you are reading Philip asked
verses.literalPt: E, correndo Filipe, ouviu que lia o profeta Isaías, e disse: Entendes tu o que lês?

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Πῶς γὰρ ἂν δυναίμην ἐὰν μή τις ὁδηγήσει με παρεκάλεσέν τε τὸν Φίλιππον ἀναβάντα καθίσαι σὺν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Ho de eipen Pōs gar an dynaimēn ean mē tis hodēgēsei me parekalesen te ton Philippon anabanta kathisai syn autō
verses.literal: How can I - he said unless . . . someone guides me And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him
verses.literalPt: E ele disse: Como poderei entender, se alguém não me ensinar? E rogou a Filipe que subisse e com ele se assentasse.

verses.original: Ἡ δὲ περιοχὴ τῆς γραφῆς ἣν ἀνεγίνωσκεν ἦν αὕτη Ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος οὕτως οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Hē de periochē tēs graphēs hēn aneginōsken ēn hautē Hōs probaton epi sphagēn ēchthē kai hōs amnos enantion tou keirantos auton aphōnos houtōs ouk anoigei to stoma autou
verses.literal: The eunuch was reading . . . this passage of Scripture He was led like a sheep to the slaughter and as a lamb before the shearer . . . is silent so He did not open His mouth
verses.literalPt: E o lugar da Escritura que lia era este: Foi levado como a ovelha para o matadouro; e, como está mudo o cordeiro diante do que o tosquia, Assim não abriu a sua boca.

verses.original: Ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει αὐτοῦ ἡ κρίσις αὐτοῦ ἤρθη τὴν γενεὰν αὐτοῦ τίς διηγήσεται ὅτι αἴρεται ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: En tē tapeinōsei autou hē krisis autou ērthē tēn genean autou tis diēgēsetai hoti airetai apo tēs gēs hē zōē autou
verses.literal: In His humiliation He was deprived of justice Who can recount His descendants For His life was removed from the earth
verses.literalPt: Na sua humilhação foi tirado o seu julgamento; E quem contará a sua geração? Porque a sua vida é tirada da terra.

verses.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ εὐνοῦχος τῷ Φιλίππῳ εἶπεν Δέομαί σου περὶ τίνος ὁ προφήτης λέγει τοῦτο περὶ ἑαυτοῦ ἢ περὶ ἑτέρου τινός
verses.transliteration: Apokritheis de ho eunouchos tō Philippō eipen Deomai sou peri tinos ho prophētēs legei touto peri heautou ē peri heterou tinos
verses.literal: Tell me . . . - said - the eunuch who is the prophet talking . . . about himself or someone else
verses.literalPt: E, respondendo o eunuco a Filipe, disse: Rogo-te, de quem diz isto o profeta? De si mesmo, ou de algum outro?

verses.original: Ἀνοίξας δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς γραφῆς ταύτης εὐηγγελίσατο αὐτῷ τὸν Ἰησοῦν
verses.transliteration: Anoixas de ho Philippos to stoma autou kai arxamenos apo tēs graphēs tautēs euēngelisato autō ton Iēsoun
verses.literal: Then Philip began with this very Scripture and - told him the good news about . . . Jesus
verses.literalPt: Então Filipe, abrindo a sua boca, e começando nesta Escritura, lhe anunciou a Jesus.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐπορεύοντο κατὰ τὴν ὁδόν ἦλθον ἐπί τι ὕδωρ καί φησιν ὁ εὐνοῦχος Ἰδοὺ ὕδωρ τί κωλύει με βαπτισθῆναι
verses.transliteration: Hōs de eporeuonto kata tēn hodon ēlthon epi ti hydōr kai phēsin ho eunouchos Idou hydōr ti kōlyei me baptisthēnai
verses.literal: As they traveled along the road and came to some water the eunuch said Look here is water What is there to prevent me from being baptized
verses.literalPt: E, indo eles caminhando, chegaram ao pé de alguma água, e disse o eunuco: Eis aqui água; que impede que eu seja batizado?
E disse Filipe: É lícito, se crês de todo o coração. E, respondendo ele, disse: Creio que Jesus Cristo é o Filho de Deus.

verses.original: καὶ ἐκέλευσεν στῆναι τὸ ἅρμα καὶ κατέβησαν ἀμφότεροι εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ ὅ τε Φίλιππος καὶ ὁ εὐνοῦχος καὶ ἐβάπτισεν αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: kai ekeleusen stēnai to harma kai katebēsan amphoteroi eis to hydōr ho te Philippos kai ho eunouchos kai ebaptisen auton
verses.literal: And he gave orders to stop the chariot Then both - Philip and the eunuch went down into the water and Philip baptized him
verses.literalPt: E mandou parar o carro, e desceram ambos à água, tanto Filipe como o eunuco, e o batizou.

verses.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἀνέβησαν ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος Πνεῦμα Κυρίου ἥρπασεν τὸν Φίλιππον καὶ οὐκ εἶδεν αὐτὸν οὐκέτι ὁ εὐνοῦχος ἐπορεύετο γὰρ τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ χαίρων
verses.transliteration: Hote de anebēsan ek tou hydatos Pneuma Kyriou hērpasen ton Philippon kai ouk eiden auton ouketi ho eunouchos eporeueto gar tēn hodon autou chairōn
verses.literal: When they came up out of the water the Spirit of the Lord carried Philip away and the eunuch saw him no more but went on his way rejoicing
verses.literalPt: E, quando saíram da água, o Espírito do Senhor arrebatou a Filipe, e não o viu mais o eunuco; e, jubiloso, continuou o seu caminho.

verses.original: Φίλιππος δὲ εὑρέθη εἰς Ἄζωτον καὶ διερχόμενος εὐηγγελίζετο τὰς πόλεις πάσας ἕως τοῦ ἐλθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς Καισάρειαν
verses.transliteration: Philippos de heurethē eis Azōton kai dierchomenos euēngelizeto tas poleis pasas heōs tou elthein auton eis Kaisareian
verses.literal: But Philip appeared at Azotus and traveled through that region preaching the gospel in all the towns until he came to Caesarea
verses.literalPt: E Filipe se achou em Azoto e, indo passando, anunciava o evangelho em todas as cidades, até que chegou a Cesaréia.
